A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CATCH and contain complete, readable 29-page papers, including Appendices A-D. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendix material support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, sensitivity analyses, and case studies in Section 4 and Appendices B-D.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark tables and Appendix D's frequency-specific anomaly experiments.

M1.justification: Equation (9) changes the specified clustering loss from exp(score)/tau to exp(score/tau) in both numerator and denominator. This is a limited revision to the documented objective; the architecture and bi-level optimization procedure remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that the implementation changed or experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 real-world and 12 synthetic benchmark datasets, plus the same four frequency-specific synthetic scenarios in Appendix D.

E2.justification: Table 2 and Appendix C retain the same 15 baselines. Appendix D retains the same comparison against ModernTCN, iTransformer, DualTF, and TFAD; no comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same evaluation metrics, dataset sizes, window and patch settings, baseline hyperparameter searches, and testing policy disabling Drop Last. No evaluation protocol revision is reported.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3, sensitivity analyses in Figure 4, anomaly-score case studies in Figures 5-6, and frequency-band experiments in Appendix D are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate and average reporting, without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and rankings in Tables 2-3 and 5-11, and the plotted findings in Figures 4-7, remain unchanged. The equation correction is not accompanied by revised empirical results.

T1.justification: Equation (9) receives a non-equivalent mathematical correction: tau cancels between numerator and denominator in v4, whereas placing it inside the exponentials in v5 makes the defined loss temperature-dependent. Other mathematical definitions remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about frequency patching, adaptive channel correlations, bi-level optimization, and state-of-the-art anomaly detection.

C2.justification: The interpretations of channel correlation, frequency modeling, and anomaly scoring remain unchanged. Both retain the Section 4.1 limitation concerning SWAT anomalies extending beyond the supported look-back window.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same software, hardware, optimizer, batch-size policy, baseline hyperparameters, optimization pseudocode, scoring implementation, and synthetic-data generation instructions. Code and dataset access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The citations, reference list, and positioning relative to channel-independent, channel-dependent, and frequency-domain approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp changes from v4 dated 8 May 2025 to v5 dated 20 June 2026. The prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 is horizontally recentered, some equations receive spacing or font-size adjustments, and Algorithm 3 changes docstring coloring and displayed spaces. Figures and tables retain their content and organization.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation (9) resolves the mismatch between calling tau a temperature coefficient and a formula in which it cancels, improving the mathematical specification of the training objective. The empirical evidence and substantive exposition remain unchanged, so the supported overall gain is limited.
